name: The Gryphon

temperament.summary: Bluff, lazy, irreverent and impatient; a hearty old hand who laughs at his betters behind their backs and bosses the child in front of her. Quick to boredom, quick to excitement.
temperament.under_pressure: Bored impatience: cuts people off and hustles them along. At a spectacle: leaps and shouts.

traits.description: He obeys the Queen to her face, then chuckles once she is out of sight and tells Alice the executions are all her fancy.

evidence.note: Watches the Queen out of sight, then chuckles: 'What fun!'

evidence.quote: It’s all her fancy, that: they never executes nobody, you know. Come on!

traits.description: He has no time for explanations. He cuts people off, gives orders and drags Alice away mid-song.

evidence.note: Interrupts 'in a very decided tone' to move on from lessons.
Takes Alice by the hand and hurries off without waiting for the end of the song.

traits.description: Joins the Mock Turtle in shaming her simple questions and calls her a simpleton. He takes on the role of the one with authority over Alice.

evidence.note: 'You ought to be ashamed of yourself for asking such a simple question'.
The Mock Turtle looks to him as if he has authority over Alice.
Orders her to stand up and recite.

traits.description: Crude but loyal to his sad friend: he thumps him on the back to get his voice back and calls him 'old fellow'.

evidence.note: Shakes him and punches him in the back when sobs choke him.
Sighs in his turn and hides his face with the Mock Turtle over the old master.

traits.description: Lazy until there is a spectacle; then he bounds into the air and yells the Quadrille figures at the top of his voice, and he is first off to the trial.

evidence.note: Shouts 'The lobsters!' with a bound into the air.
Yells at the top of his voice.
'Come on!' at the first cry of the trial.

traits.description: Found asleep in the sun, and the Queen calls him 'lazy thing'. He never learned the Drawling-master's 'Fainting in Coils' because he 'hadn't time', and he has forgotten the song words.

evidence.note: Lying fast asleep in the sun; 'Up, lazy thing!'
The Mock Turtle: 'the Gryphon never learnt it.'

motivation.core: Entertainment with the least effort: fun, spectacle and a good story, and no tedious explanations.
motivation.fear: Boredom, and having to exert himself for nothing.
motivation.wants_from_alice: An audience for the Quadrille and a good story from her, in that order.

shifts.to: amused escort, showing the child the Mock Turtle for fun
shifts.trigger: the Queen's order, and the joke of her empty threats

shifts.from: master of ceremonies at the shore
shifts.to: hurrying to the trial, the bigger show

habits.habit: Waits until authority has left before showing what he thinks
Grabs the child by the hand and hurries off without explanation
Throws both paws (hands) up in exaggerated surprise
Whispers a knowing aside to Alice at public occasions
Sprawls and lounges wherever he stops, like a big cat in the sun
habits.reason: Extends the source's sleeping-in-the-sun image into the lion hindquarters' natural sprawl for the photoreal CGI griffin (SUP-010 as amended by BIB-0027).

decision_pattern: Chooses whatever is more fun right now and cuts off anything slow. He treats orders from above lightly but carries them out.

taboos.taboo: Never takes the Queen's threats seriously, and never sides with her against anyone
Never sits through a long explanation
Never mocks the Queen to her face; his irreverence only comes out when she is gone

facade.surface: The Queen's obedient servant, roused from sleep to do her bidding
facade.true_self: A cheerful cynic who knows the Queen's death sentences are never carried out
facade.reveal_note: The reveal is the chuckle at ch009-p44 to ch009-p46, the key line behind SUP-014. Blocking: he must be deadpan and obedient until the Queen is fully out of frame.

waking_life_embodiment.embodies: The bluff senior servant, groom or old gardener told to 'take the young lady' somewhere: rough-spoken, bossy with the child, and privately scornful of the mistress's tantrums.
waking_life_embodiment.waking_source: The servants of the family and the neighbouring farm. The sister's reverie links his shriek to the farmyard clamour (ch012-p70, cp-sounds). His ungrammatical speech marks him as working-class in a scholar's household.
waking_life_embodiment.authority_trait: Delegated authority: the adult charged with minding a child, who treats her as a simpleton, yet tells her the truth the gentry will not, that the threats are empty.
waking_life_embodiment.coming_of_age_reading: He gives Alice the most useful fact in the dream: 'they never executes nobody'. Adult threats are bluster. She carries that knowledge into the trial, where it lets her stand up at full size. He also shows her that grown-ups who boss her about are just as bored and silly as she is.
waking_life_embodiment.reason: The empty-threats line and the farmyard sound link are sourced. Casting him as a senior servant or groom is a design reading for the realistic frame.

performance_baseline: Photoreal CGI griffin (SUP-010, BIB-0027): big, loose-limbed, heavy-lidded, then suddenly explosive. Eagle head cocks and snaps, neck feathers rouse when amused, the lion tail lashes, wings half-mantle when he bosses Alice about. The voice is a rough burr; the shriek is a sound-design cue linked to the farmyard.
